overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated videos reveals a clear performance divergence: high-stakes, first-person immersive 'What If You Fell Into...' cosmic/exoplanet survival scenarios consistently generate top-tier reach (800-1,000+ views, 20-38 likes), while abstract psychology concepts and repetitive re-uploads ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'Why Space Is Completely Silent') suffer severe viewer fatigue, stagnating under 50 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Survival Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) dramatically outperformed third-person factual formats.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor future scripts around first-person visceral peril, walking the viewer step-by-step through catastrophic environmental physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos at 19-21s detailing extreme physical anomalies (TrES-2b at 1,030 views, Venus Day/Year at 981 views, Supersonic Rubies at 725 views) dominate engagement metrics compared to sub-16s clips.
winning_patterns.action: Maintain optimal runtime between 19-22 seconds to allow pacing for a tension buildup and mid-point scientific twist.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-10 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) consistently generated lowest retention and zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Pause generic brain/neurology trivia unless framed as high-stakes mystery or psychological horror micro-narratives.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' dropped from 220 views to 34 views, showing diminishing returns.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict deduplication; do not re-cover identical topics or titles within 30-day windows.
